text: Arguments outside 0..str.length or not integers are not checked (Q9). Forward from pos > length returns pos + 2 (codePointAt gives NaN, codePointSize(NaN) is 2), so findClusterBreak("ab", 5) is 7 and findClusterBreak("", 1) is 3. Forward from a negative pos, the first step adds 2 (the code unit at a negative index is NaN, size 2); while the position is still negative, each code unit read is NaN, which isExtendingChar reports as extending (every comparison with NaN is false, so its binary search ends in `return true`), so with includeExtending true it is absorbed two units at a time until the position reaches 0 or 1, and the scan then goes on from there. Odd negative positions reach 1 without reading index 0 ("ab" from -1, -3, -5, -7 is 1; "\u{1F600}a" from -1 or -3 is 1, inside the surrogate pair); even ones reach 0 and take index 0 as the next code point, so the result is 0 unless index 0 holds a table code point or a ZWJ ("ab" from -2 is 0, "\u0301ab" from -2 is 1) (F0097, F0098, F6097, F7022-F7028, F7035). With includeExtending false NaN is not absorbed and the scan stops after the first step: -1 gives 1, -2 gives 0, every pos <= -3 gives pos + 2, a negative result (F7029-F7031, F7035). The empty string behaves the same (F7032-F7035). Backward from pos > length returns length, for every length (F0099, F0100, F0149, F7036); backward from a negative pos returns 0 (B12, F7036). A fractional pos gives fractional results (1.5 -> 2.5 forward, 0.5 backward) because charCodeAt truncates the index; NaN forward returns NaN, NaN backward returns 0.

text: A tab (code unit 9) moves the column to the next multiple of tabSize: n += tabSize - (n % tabSize); a tab at a tab stop advances a full tabSize. The tab is stepped by one code unit (i++).

Every other grapheme cluster counts one column, found with findClusterBreak(string, i) (includeExtending true): an astral code point (2 units), a base with marks, a ZWJ sequence, a flag pair, a wide CJK character and each of CR, LF, U+2028 all count 1. There is no East Asian width and no zero-width case; Hangul jamo count one each (findClusterBreak B9).

A `to` that falls inside a cluster (between surrogate halves, between a base and its mark) counts that whole cluster: the test i < to is made at the cluster start. `to` inside a tab is not possible (a tab is one unit); `to` = 0 is column 0.
hazards: A `to` inside a character is accepted; its column is that of the end of the cluster (D1).

text: `to` outside 0..length: past the end the count stops at the string length (fixed in 6.5.1, mirrors/cm6/state/CHANGELOG.md:75, which reports an infinite loop before); negative or NaN `to` gives 0; a fractional `to` counts every cluster starting below it (countColumn("abc", 4, 1.5) is 2).
hazards: Fractional and NaN `to` accepted silently (Q9).

text: tabSize outside the positive integers is not checked (Q9): tabSize 0 gives NaN after the first tab (n % 0 is NaN) and keeps it NaN; a string without tabs is unaffected; negative tabSize makes the column negative (countColumn("\t", -4) is -4); a fractional tabSize gives fractional columns; NaN tabSize gives NaN after a tab.
hazards: NaN result; negative and fractional results; JS numbers (Q9).

text: A tab followed by a code point of the extending table (Extend or SpacingMark below U+30000, findClusterBreak B5) or a ZWJ: the tab is stepped by one code unit (B2), so the following code point starts a cluster of its own and counts one column (countColumn("\t\u0301x", 4) is 6, with to = 2 it is 5; countColumn("\t\u093fx", 4) is 6, F7019). findColumn steps the same tab with findClusterBreak, which absorbs the mark into the tab, so the two functions disagree on such strings (findColumn B8, Q23).
hazards: countColumn and findColumn are not inverse on a tab followed by a code point of the extending table (Extend or SpacingMark) or ZWJ (Q23).

text: A tab that follows a ZWJ is inside the ZWJ's cluster (findClusterBreak joins the code point after a ZWJ), so the tab test, made only at cluster starts, does not see it: it counts as part of a one-column cluster with no tab-stop advance (countColumn("a\u200D\tb", 4) is 2; with to = 3 it is 1).
hazards: Tabs inside clusters are not tab stops.

text: Walks clusters from 0, adding 1 per non-tab cluster, and returns the offset i of the first cluster boundary where the column n reaches col (n >= col).

text: A col that falls inside a tab's span (between the tab's start column and its tab stop) returns the offset after the tab: the tab adds tabSize - n % tabSize at once and the next check sees n >= col.

Offsets are cluster boundaries from findClusterBreak (includeExtending true): an astral code point, a base with marks, a ZWJ sequence and a flag pair are stepped over whole, so the result is never inside one.
String too short to reach col: returns string.length, or -1 when strict === true. Only the boolean true selects -1; strict false, undefined or a truthy non-boolean (1) return the length.

strict compared with === true, so a truthy non-boolean behaves as false.

text: A col equal to the column reached at the end of the string returns string.length even with strict, because n >= col is tested before i == string.length; a col inside the last tab's span also returns the length with strict.

Arguments outside the domain are not checked (Q9): tabSize 0 turns n into NaN at the first tab and no later n >= col succeeds, so the result is the length (or -1 strict); negative tabSize gives offsets without error; fractional col is reached at the first n >= col (findColumn("abc", 1.5, 4) is 2); NaN and Infinity col never match and return the length (or -1 strict).

text: The categorizer checks in a fixed order, each over the whole string: (1) no non-whitespace character (/\S/ fails) gives Space; (2) any \p{Alphabetic}, \p{Number} or `_` code point anywhere gives Word; (3) any code unit of the language data `wordChars` contained in the string gives Word; (4) otherwise Other. So "a b" is Word, " -" is Other, and wordChars cannot turn a whitespace-only string into Word.
hazards: Unicode data of the JS engine (Q7): \p{Alphabetic}, \p{Number} and /\S/ come from the runtime (fixtures record node 22.23.4, Unicode 17.0, ICU 78.3).
stack: Mechanism: step (3) iterates `wordChars` by index (`wordChars[i]`, mirrors/cm6/state/src/charcategory.ts:32), so it matches UTF-16 code units, not characters (as recorded for state.CharCategory.Word.B6); step (2) is the `\p{Alphabetic}\p{Number}_` RegExp only when the engine compiles it: a try/catch (mirrors/cm6/state/src/charcategory.ts:15-16) falls back to the /\w/ and case-comparison test of hasWordChar (mirrors/cm6/state/src/charcategory.ts:13, :18-25) on engines that reject \p{...}. Evidence: code structure, the try/catch; no CHANGELOG entry found. Exists because JS strings are UTF-16 (step 3) and for backward compatibility with older JS engines (step 2); editor need underneath: word, space and other categories for word motion and selection.
cost: linear in the string length plus the wordChars length times the string length (indexOf per wordChars code unit)

text: A Line is a plain object with four data fields (from, to, number, text) and a length getter, created by Text.lineAt and Text.line on every call: two queries for the same line return distinct objects (doc.line(1) !== doc.line(1)), so Line identity carries no meaning. Its constructor is @internal; instanceof Line holds for every returned value.
hazards: Object identity: a fresh object per query; no caller may rely on ===.
Fields are writable at runtime (TypeScript readonly only); length is recomputed from them (F0822).

Editor need underneath: describing a line without storing per-line objects in a large document. Allocation per call relies on a garbage collector (deduction).
cost: O(log n) per query (the lookup); the object itself O(1) plus a reference to the stored line string

text: Position of the first code unit of the line, in UTF-16 code units: 0 for line 1, and the previous line's to + 1 for every later line (each line break takes exactly one position, whatever separator the source text used). Astral characters count 2 positions; CR and U+2028 stored inside a line are ordinary content.
Position at the end of the line's content, before its line break: from + text.length in UTF-16 code units.
For the last line, to equals the document length (there is no break after it); for an empty last line from == to == length.

1-based line number: 1 for the first line, lines for the last; from lineAt(pos) it is the number of breaks before pos plus one, where a pos at a line's end (just before its break) belongs to that line.
The line's content without any line break, the same string the document stores (no copy is made); "" for an empty line. CR and U+2028 inside a line given to Text.of are content.
hazards: Aliasing: the string is the stored one (immutable in JS, so not observable).

text: Three implementations share the interface: the raw cursor (Text.iter), the partial cursor (Text.iterRange) and the line cursor (Text.iterLines). Each is its own iterable: [Symbol.iterator]() returns the cursor itself, so for..of and spread continue from the current state and a second spread yields nothing. next() returns the cursor itself, which serves as the iterator-protocol result object ({value, done}).
hazards: Duck-typed protocol: the cursor is its own IteratorResult; the same object is returned by every next().
Mutable shared state: iterating with for..of consumes the cursor.
stack: Mechanism: the cursor doubles as the JS IteratorResult and is installed on prototypes only when Symbol exists (`if (typeof Symbol != "undefined")`, mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:554). Evidence: that guard (backward compatibility with engines without Symbol) and the structure; no CHANGELOG entry found. Editor need underneath: sequential reading of the document.

text: Before the first next(): value is "", done is false, lineBreak is false, for all three cursors and both directions.

Raw forward cursor (iter() or iter(1)), next() without skip: yields each non-empty line's whole content and "
" for each line break, in document order, then done. Empty lines yield nothing of their own (two consecutive breaks show as two "
"); the empty document is done at the first call. Values never span a line break; a "
" stored inside a line (Q9) is part of a line value with lineBreak false. Whole lines are returned, never split at leaf or node boundaries.
hazards: Empty lines produce no value: callers count positions from value lengths (DocInput, lint, view) and see breaks only.
stack: Mechanism: the JS iterator protocol: `TextIterator` extends `Iterator<string>, Iterable<string>` (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:15), and `next` returns the cursor itself, which doubles as the IteratorResult (`done`, `value` fields on the cursor, mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:16-25; RawTextCursor mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:403-405, :425-428), so one mutable object is reused for every step; the `[Symbol.iterator]` methods are installed only when `Symbol` exists (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:554-558). Evidence: code structure and that guard; no CHANGELOG entry found. Editor need underneath: sequential reading of the document without allocating a result per step.
cost: amortized O(1) per value (a stack of nodes, one entry per tree level)

text: Raw reverse cursor (iter(-1)): yields the same values in reverse order (the strings themselves are not reversed): last line first, "\n" for each break, empty lines skipped.

Raw cursor, next(skip) with skip > 0: the cursor's position p is the end of the previous value (forward; the start for reverse), 0 (length for reverse) before the first call. Forward it reads at q = p + skip: done (value "") when q >= length; "\n" when q is a line-break position; otherwise the rest of the line from q (which can start or end inside a surrogate pair, giving a lone surrogate, F0843). Reverse reads at q = p - skip: done when q <= 0; "\n" when q - 1 is a break; otherwise the part of the line before q. Skips cross whole tree children without visiting them when skip exceeds the child's length. Checked against this model on 300 seeded cases (gen-text.ts).
hazards: UTF-16: a skip can land inside a surrogate pair and the value then starts or ends with a lone surrogate.
stack: Mechanism: skip counts UTF-16 code units and the value is cut with `String.prototype.slice` (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:443-445), which works on code units, so a skip that ends inside a surrogate pair yields a lone surrogate (F0843). Evidence: code structure. Editor need underneath: reading the document from a position.

The range is not clipped to the document (Text.iterRange B2). done is set when a step produces an empty value (done = !value). Values can start or end inside a surrogate pair (F0864).

Before the first step pos is the document length, so to - pos is negative and a positive skip turns into a negative one: iterRange(12, 2).next(2) returns "four" (positions 15-19, outside the range), iterRange(6, 2) on "abcdefgh" with next(1) returns "cdefgh" (positions 2-8), iterRange(8, 2).next(1) ignores the skip (F0870, F0872, F0873). After the first step a positive skip is limited by the distance already travelled (to - pos) rather than the distance left, and a negative skip by from - pos (F0871). Q24.

text: Line cursor (iterLines), next() without skip: yields each line's content once, "" for every empty line including empty lines at the end of the range and the single line of the empty document, never "\n"; then done. Implemented over an inner raw or partial cursor: a break directly after a line is consumed by a recursive next(), a break after a break (or at the start) yields "", and the end after a break yields one final "" (CHANGELOG 6.3.2, mirrors/cm6/state/CHANGELOG.md:113).
hazards: Recursion: next() calls itself once per line break (depth 1).

Values built by ChangeSet.of, compose and map go through addSection, which (in this order) drops a section with len 0 and ins <= 0; extends the previous section's len when ins <= 0 equals the previous ins (adjacent unchanged spans merge, adjacent deletions merge: deleting 2-4 and 4-6 of 8 gives the sections (2,-1),(4,0),(2,-1)); adds ins to the previous section when len is 0 and the previous len is 0 (insertions at one point merge); joins into the previous section when forceJoin; otherwise appends. So adjacent replacements stay separate ([[1,'A'],[1,'B'],1]), and a deletion followed by an insertion at its end, or an insertion followed by a deletion at the same point, stay two sections.

text: In a touched chunk, an empty range maps its start with mapPos(pos, startSide, mapMode) and is dropped on null (RangeValue.mapMode.B1); the side decides before/after an insertion at the position (RangeValue.startSide.B3).

In a touched chunk, an empty range with startSide != endSide also maps its end with endSide (Simple); it is dropped when the end maps before the start, and when it stays empty with endSide < startSide (RangeValue.endSide.B3, B4).

In a touched chunk, a non-empty range maps from with startSide and to with endSide (Simple mode, never null); it is dropped when newFrom > newTo, or when it collapses to empty and endSide < startSide (RangeValue.endSide.B4); otherwise it is kept, possibly empty. Inclusive ends grow with insertions at them, exclusive ones do not (RangeValue.endSide.B2).

Mapped ranges are re-laid within the chunk: a range that still starts at or after the previous kept end (with sides) is appended; an empty one that falls before it is reinserted at the last earlier slot where it fits, scanning backwards while the earlier range does not start after it; anything else is spilled to a new layer. The new chunk starts at the first mapped range's new from (also when that range is spilled) and holds positions relative to it; its maxPoint is recomputed from the kept points; a chunk with no kept range is removed. Examples: points a(1, startSide 1), b(2, startSide -1) deleting [1,2] -> b, a both at 1 in two layers; [0,3] sides -1/1 with a TrackDel point at 5 (side -1) and a point at 6 (side 0) deleting [3,6] -> the point at 5 is dropped, the point at 6 lands at 3 in a second layer; [0,4]/(point 5) deleting [3,5] -> point at 3 spilled.
